headline: HG deal lifts volumes, but acquisition debt squeezes profit
summary_short: Revenue rose 7.1% y/y to $327M as throughput from the HG Acquisition and CPI-based rate escalators more than offset the Utica Shale Divestiture, but diluted EPS fell to $0.24 from $0.26 as higher interest expense on acquisition debt outpaced operating gains.
summary_long: Q2 2026 revenue grew 7.1% y/y to $327M, led by HG Acquisition gathering and compression throughput plus annual CPI escalators, partly offset by the Utica Shale Divestiture and natural well decline. Direct operating expenses jumped 34% on HG-related costs, pulling operating income down 2.4% to $182M despite the revenue gain. Interest expense rose 16% to $56M on 2033/2034 Notes issued for the $1.1B HG Acquisition, driving net income down 8.8% to $114M and diluted EPS to $0.24 from $0.26. Long-term debt rose 17.9% to $3.57B on the acquisition financing. The company paid a $0.225/share dividend, repurchased $8M of stock, and restated its FY2026 capital budget of $190-220M first announced in February 2026.

drivers.explanation: HG Acquisition added gathering, compression and water throughput plus CPI-based rate escalators; partially offset by the Utica Shale Divestiture and natural well decline.
Direct operating expenses rose 34% y/y on HG Acquisition-related gathering, well pad compression and water handling costs, outpacing the 7% revenue gain.
Roughly flat y/y — higher depreciation add-back from HG Acquisition assets offsets the operating-income decline, leaving EBITDA about 1% higher.
Interest expense rose 16% y/y to $56M from the 2033/2034 Notes issued to fund the HG Acquisition, compounding the operating-income decline.
Mirrors the net income decline; diluted weighted-average share count was roughly flat y/y (477.1M vs 482.5M).
2033 and 2034 Notes issued in the second half of 2025 funded the $1.1B HG Acquisition, partially offset by redemption of the 2027 Notes.
Not directly addressed in the release; consistent with the $0.225/share dividend and $8M of quarterly buybacks reducing retained equity faster than net income rebuilds it.

The quarter is a volume story, not a margin story: HG Acquisition throughput drove the top line, while the debt raised to fund that same acquisition consumed the operating gain at the net-income line.
